verdict.root_cause: Six minutes before the 13:07:45 alert, platform automation set OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT on paymentservice to a loopback address, and unlike the three earlier applications of the same variable this one was never reverted [tr_8a66c0eabb4e]. With the exporter pointed at a port where no collector listens, paymentservice spans never reach the trace backend — Tempo holds zero traces for the service [tr_377af1a1ab1b] — and the span-derived calls_total series the error-ratio query depends on is empty in both incident and baseline windows [tr_02a51f7ee8d6, tr_4f92ce2f10dc]. Meanwhile the business path is healthy: paymentservice logs show continuous charge/complete pairs completing sub-millisecond through 13:09:51 [tr_efe29a065740], and checkoutservice shows complete order flows with advancing queue offsets and 14–20 ms payment latency at window close [tr_c05acdab65ba]. The wrong endpoint value is itself the failing thing: it silently discards the service's telemetry, which is what the alert is reacting to.
verdict.reasoning: Traces are wholly absent rather than sparse [tr_377af1a1ab1b] and the error-ratio series is empty [tr_02a51f7ee8d6], yet both paymentservice and its caller log healthy, fast, completing transactions at window close [tr_efe29a065740, tr_c05acdab65ba]. A genuine payment failure would surface in the caller, which is the service that notices first; it does not. The only recorded change is repeated toggling of one variable, the OTLP traces endpoint, with the pre-onset application uniquely lacking a revert [tr_8a66c0eabb4e] — that asymmetry distinguishes this occurrence from the three earlier incident-free ones. Not bad_deploy: no deployment or image record exists in the window. Not dependency_latency: nothing waited, latencies are sub-millisecond.
open_questions: Which signal actually fired the 13:07:45 alert was never retrieved, so the link between empty telemetry and the page is inferred rather than observed.
Both log queries were truncated and omitted roughly 12:38–13:07:57 [tr_efe29a065740, tr_c05acdab65ba], so a short self-healing degradation at onset is not excluded.

Trace absence spans 100+ minutes predating the 13:01 change [tr_377af1a1ab1b] while the variable was reportedly reverted at 09:40, so a longer-standing instrumentation or label/tenant mismatch may explain the gap instead; calls_total was never tried under any other selector.

alternatives.root_cause: paymentservice traces and metrics never existed under the queried names due to a standing instrumentation or label mismatch, and the alert is a monitoring artifact unrelated to the 13:01 change.
alternatives.why_not: Fails to explain why an alert fired at 13:07:45 specifically, six minutes after the one un-reverted application of the endpoint variable; the change timing is the only thing on the board correlated with onset.

alternatives.root_cause: A brief real degradation on the charge path occurred around 13:07:45 and recovered before the retained log lines resume at 13:07:57.
alternatives.why_not: No error or timeout line appears anywhere in either service's returned logs, and checkout's payment latency is unchanged at both ends of the window; the hypothesis survives only inside the truncated gap and has no positive evidence.

retrieved:
/ Confirming it: The change record shows the variable and both values. A configuration pointing at an address
that no longer answers usually produces connection errors in the service's own logs with the
address quoted verbatim - the fastest confirmation available, because the wrong value appears

/ Blast radius: One service - with one exception worth naming explicitly. Where the reverted value is a
dependency address, the services it was pointing at see traffic move. That is a second-order
effect on a service nobody alerted on, and it belongs in the proposal.

/ Blast radius, and the one irreversible property: One service, for the duration of the recreate. **This action is not reversible** - it discards
in-process state, which for this world's services is cache only. Say so in the proposal rather
than leaving the approver to know it.

proposal.expected_effect: No action taken. The proposed config_revert does not fit the evidence: Tempo holds zero paymentservice traces uniformly from 11:07:45, and that result explicitly rules out a pipeline break starting at 13:01 [tr_377af1a1ab1b], so reverting a 13:01 endpoint change cannot restore spans already absent for 100+ minutes prior. The empty calls_total series is separately explained as a selector/label mismatch, since service_name='paymentservice' returns nothing over four hours and is called unusable [tr_4f92ce2f10dc]. Meanwhile the business path is healthy [tr_efe29a065740], so there is no user-visible symptom for a revert to fix. Correct next step is investigation, not remediation: re-query calls_total under the app/job label or 'payment-service', and retrieve the actual alert rule that fired at 13:07:45.
proposal.if_wrong: If a re-query of calls_total under a corrected selector shows a real series that goes empty only after 13:01, and Tempo shows paymentservice spans under a different service name before 13:01, then the endpoint change is causal and revert_config on paymentservice becomes justified.
proposal.risk: Abstaining leaves a misconfigured OTLP endpoint in place, so paymentservice telemetry stays blind and a genuine future fault on the charge path may go unobserved. The drift loop [tr_8a66c0eabb4e] may also reapply the value regardless of any manual revert.
proposal.blast_radius: No change, so nobody sees anything. Had the revert proceeded, paymentservice would have been recreated, with checkoutservice (and frontend behind it) seeing reset connections on the charge path during a period when both are confirmed healthy.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A single critical alert on paymentservice, a payment-path service with downstream checkout and frontend exposure, is not something to dismiss without evidence. No signal yet distinguishes deploy, config, or resource causes.
